paradoxes.text: The tie that earns Paraguay Taipei's visits and its place in Taiwan's diplomacy is also what isolates it in the region: its main diplomatic currency is its main regional cost. Our reading (C); the sources read give the recognition and the pressure, not the Mercosur or trade figures.

grand_strategy.reading: Paraguay plays one card: recognition of Taipei, the only South American state that still holds it, which buys a state visit with military honours and a place in Taiwan's diplomacy. Beijing's pressure to switch is the constant test of that card, and the Triple Frontier allegations, which Paraguay shares with Washington, are its second security file. The card is thin: the sources read cover the Taiwan tie and the security allegations, not Brazil, Argentina, the United States, Israel, the EU, soy, beef or hydropower, which stay open until read.

stances.note: Partner by recognition, not ally: no defence clause. Mirrors the TWN card's stance toward PRY (same sources, same bond). Peña's state visit to Taipei from 7 May 2026, with a military welcome and a meeting with Lai, and his call for Taiwan as a 'fundamental partner' (AP via Arab News) are the statement; the grade stays partner. Bond affinity: anti-communism and a shared democratic frame, as the TWN card reads it. Trend stable: the visit is the reaffirmation of an existing tie, not a move.

stances.note: Our reading, C: Paraguay keeps no diplomatic relations with Beijing, and Beijing presses it to switch recognition, which is competing interests with friction. The grade is rival, not adversary: nothing read points to Beijing's defeat or disappearance as Asunción's aim. No source read uses the word rival for this pair, so it rests on the AP reporting of the pressure. Bond none: no shared identity and no open grievance. The soy and beef trade with China, through third parties, is not read yet and is not in the grade. Since: the date of Paraguay's recognition of the Republic of China, as the start of the tie that Beijing contests.

stances_toward.note: Peña and Milei share the right-of-centre line: Paraguay was among the ten states that voted with Argentina against the General Assembly endorsement of the two-state New York Declaration on 12 Sep 2025 (UN News, mirrored from the PSE card), hosted the Mercosur summit of 29-30 June 2026, and Peña travelled to Buenos Aires in July 2026 to meet Milei. The irritants are shared-resource ones: the Yacyreta binational entity (Milei replaced its Argentine director) and the tolls and privatisation of the Parana-Paraguay waterway, on which Paraguayan commentary is critical (a single press digest; not checked at source). No treaty, so partner, not ally. Bond affinity: our reading from the voting line (C). Trend stable. Itaipu not covered.

stances_toward.note: Partner bound by Itaipu: the binational dam (1973 treaty) makes the two states each other's largest energy counterpart, and the review of Annex C, the financial bases, falls due 50 years after entry into force. Lula and Pena met in Brasilia on 15 July 2026 with Itaipu the main item, after ministers met in Asuncion in March; Paraguay wants to sell its surplus on the Brazilian free market, Brazil wants a tariff without the debt burden; no signed agreement was found. Pena also said in August that the Milei-Lula crisis does not affect Mercosur, and Paraguay hosted the June 2026 summit. Not a reluctant partner: no source reads it so. Stable is our reading (C). Bond none. Paraguay is the only South American state that recognises Taipei (PRY card), while Brazil does not recognise Taiwan; this is a standing difference, not a quarrel.

stances_toward.note: Rival, and cooling from Beijing's side: the newest act is the sanction of 12 Oct 2026. In May 2026 the Foreign Ministry spokesman Lin Jian told Asuncion to 'stand on the right side of history' and to sever 'so-called diplomatic relations' with Taipei; in July the spokesman Guo Jiakun called Paraguay's leaders 'pawns of the independence forces of Taiwan'. On 12 Oct the ministry froze the assets of the communications minister Gustavo Villate and barred him from mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau, with Belize's foreign minister in the same action, for the Taiwan technology work. Paraguay answered that the sanctions create 'unnecessary friction' and reaffirmed its support for Taipei. Rival, not adversary: the sanction names ministers over their ties with Taipei, not the state, and Reuters calls it largely symbolic. Bond none. Confidence C: the MFA acts are tier 1 for what Beijing said; the rival grade is ours.

stances_toward.note: Partner by recognition (the recognition dataset holds the Paraguayan side). President Peña's four-day state visit to Taipei from 7 May 2026 (his fourth trip) came a day after Beijing asked Paraguay to 'make the right choice'; they signed agreements including an MoU on an AI computing centre. Not an ally in the ontology's sense - no defence clause - but the most reliable of the South American allies and Peña's government has so far resisted Chinese offers. Bond - affinity: anti-communism and a common democratic frame.

relations_to.summary: Itaipu, the binational dam: Brazil buys Paraguay's share of the power under the 1973 treaty, whose Annex C (the financial bases) is due for review 50 years after entry into force. One source puts the tariff at USD 19.28 per kW-month, while a January 2024 report had Brazil defending USD 16.71 and an analyst argued for USD 12-15; the sources do not agree on which figure is current. Lula and Peña met in Brasilia on 15 July 2026 with Itaipu the main item, after ministers met in Asuncion in March; Paraguay wants to sell its surplus on the Brazilian free market. No signed agreement was found; Lula reportedly will not raise the price before the vote.
